literal: Penance indeed happens to those who possess penance; those without that undertaking it (is vain).
translation: Penance is fruitful only for those who already possess the inner discipline for it. It is futile for those without that nature to undertake it.
modern: தவம் செய்யும் இயல்பு உடையவர்களுக்கே தவம் கைகூடும். அந்த இயல்பு இல்லாதவர்கள் தவத்தை மேற்கொள்வது வீணாகும்.
explanation: This couplet states that the practice of asceticism or penance cannot be forced; it requires an inherent disposition. The phrase 'தவமும் தவமுடையார்க்கு ஆகும்' means that penance naturally succeeds only for those whose minds are already conditioned for it. The second half, 'அதனை அஃதிலார் மேற்கொள்வது' (those without it undertaking it), leaves the conclusion unstated but clearly implies that such an effort is useless. The word 'ஆகும்' (will happen or succeed) in the first half sets up this contrast, showing that outward acts of penance require an inward readiness.
